$comment: THE MONEY RENDERING RULE, as a table three independent implementations must agree on.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (012 / T1211). One rule - `Equivalent.precision` is the MINIMUM number
of fraction digits a money string carries, never the maximum - is implemented three times, in
three languages, in three projects that share no module: `app/utils/money.py::to_money_str`,
`simulator-ui/v2/src/utils/money.ts::formatMoney`, and
`admin-ui/src/utils/decimal.ts::formatDecimalMinScale`. There is no npm workspace and no shared
package between the two UIs, so the duplication cannot be removed cheaply.
The duplication is not cosmetic: it was the MECHANISM of a P1. The backend and the simulator UI
carried the rule correctly while admin-ui quantized to exactly `precision` with ROUND_HALF_UP,
so `0.05` of the shipped HOUR (precision 1) - a value the door accepts and Numeric(20, 8) stores
exactly - was shown to operators as `0.1`. Three private test suites all passed. Nothing in the
tree compared the three copies to each other, so nothing could notice.
This table is that comparison. Each implementation has a test that reads THIS file and asserts
its own output against `expected`, so a copy that drifts fails in its own project, and a case
added here is answered by all three at once:
- tests/unit/test_p012_t1211_money_rendering_conformance.py
- simulator-ui/v2/src/utils/money.conformance.test.ts
- admin-ui/src/utils/decimal.conformance.test.ts
SCOPE. Valid plain decimal strings only. The three implementations deliberately differ on
malformed input (the backend raises on non-finite, admin-ui returns the input unchanged,
simulator-ui renders zero) and those differences are documented at each call site, not here.
Exponent notation is not in the table because it cannot be produced by any of the three.
ONE DIVERGENCE IS RECORDED RATHER THAN LEVELLED, and deliberately kept out of the cases: the
backend renders Decimal('-0.00') as '-0.00' where both UIs render '0.00'. It is out because
the cases are a contract all three must meet and here they do not; it is left alone because
no route through the ledger produces a signed zero - measured on PostgreSQL 16, not argued,
and pinned by tests/integration/
test_p012_t1211_negative_zero_cannot_come_back_from_the_ledger_postgres.py.
THE DOMAIN IS PART OF THE CONTRACT, NOT A CONVENIENCE SAMPLE. T1211's repeat review broke the
first version of this table by observing that its 21 cases used only precisions 0, 1, 2 and 8
out of the contract's 0..18, with negatives only at 1 and 2. Three plausible wrong
implementations passed every case: capping display precision at the storage scale 8,
supporting only the sampled precisions, and losing the sign only at precision 0. A table that
cannot tell those apart is not evidence, however many rows it has - which is why the guard
on this file is no longer a row count but a list of CLASSES it must contain (precision 0, a
precision between the sampled ones, one past the storage scale, the contract's widest, signs
at each of those, and all three scale-versus-precision relations). Adding a case is cheap;
deleting one now costs a named class.
THE DOMAIN NARROWED ON 2026-08-25 (012 / S1), AND TEN CASES CHANGED STATUS RATHER THAN
LEAVING. `Equivalent.precision` was 0..18 when this table was written; it is now 0..8,
matching `Numeric(20, 8)` and protocol §3.2 (`docs/ru/02-protocol-spec.md:155`). So the ten
cases at precision 9, 12 and 18 are no longer CONTRACT - the canon cannot produce those
calls any more. Their `why` now says so, one by one, and none of them says 'the contract'.
THEY ARE KEPT. THE FIRST REASON GIVEN HERE WAS CIRCULAR AND IS CORRECTED BELOW (2026-09-10,
closure review): deleting the rows reddens the table's OWN coverage requirements plus a mutant
kept on purpose, which shows the deletion is guarded, not that the rows are needed. The
non-circular reason is LEGACY REACHABILITY: a row written when the door accepted `precision:
12` is still in the database, ORM hydration does not re-validate it, and every producer
renders it at its own precision - so an implementation capping display at the storage scale is
wrong ON REACHABLE DATA, not merely on hypothetical input. The measurement below stands as a
measurement of the guard, and is kept for that.
THE ORIGINAL MEASUREMENT. With those ten rows deleted, the
table's own discriminating-power check (`test_the_table_can_tell_a_wrong_implementation
_apart`) stops catching `_caps_display_precision_at_the_storage_scale` ENTIRELY: 0
disagreements out of 28 remaining cases, because `min(precision, 8)` is the identity on a
0..8 domain. `_supports_only_the_historically_sampled_precisions` drops from 11
disagreements to 1, i.e. one row away from vacuous. Both are real implementations a person
could write - the first is exactly what T1211's repeat review found walking through the
table's first version. So the ten rows are the guard on the two wrong implementations the
narrowing would otherwise hide, and the three readers must keep answering them.
What that costs is honesty about their status, not the rows: all three implementations take
`precision` as a plain integer and none of them can see an `Equivalent`, so a caller passing
12 is a caller the functions still have to be right for. `to_money_str`'s own `localcontext`
sizing is pinned on the same footing (`app/utils/money.py`).
2026-09-10, CLOSURE REVIEW (gpt-6-astra, medium): THE TABLE STILL HAD A HOLE, AND IT WAS A
WHOLE CLASS OF VALUE RATHER THAN A PRECISION. Not one of the 39 cases was a nonzero integer
whose last digit is zero. So an implementation that does `text.rstrip('0').rstrip('.')` on
the ENTIRE decimal string before padding the fraction passed every single row - measured, 0
disagreements out of 39 - while rendering `120` at precision 0 as `12`. That is not a
cosmetic difference; it is a tenfold error in an amount of money, produced by a mistake a
person could plausibly make while implementing 'precision is a minimum, so strip what is
not needed'.
Five cases close it, and `_strips_trailing_zeros_before_padding` joins the control set so
the table is measured against that mistake on every run. NOTE WHAT THIS IS THE THIRD
INSTANCE OF: the domain of PRECISIONS was the hole the previous review found, and the
domain of VALUES was this one. The sample keeps being the blind spot, never the code.
rule: precision is the minimum number of fraction digits, and never fewer than the value itself needs

A NONZERO INTEGER WHOSE LAST DIGIT IS ZERO - the class this table did not contain at all until 2026-09-10, found by external review. Measured: an implementation that strips trailing zeros from the WHOLE string and then pads the fraction satisfied all 39 previous cases with zero disagreements, and renders this one as '12'. Money off by a factor of ten, invisible to the sample.
the same integer padded: the zero belongs to the magnitude, the added zeros to the fraction, and an implementation that cannot tell them apart fails exactly here
sign plus an integer ending in zero, so a magnitude-eating strip cannot hide behind the sign handling
the fraction's trailing zeros ARE dropped down to precision 0 while the magnitude's zero is not - the one case that separates 'strip what the precision does not need' from 'strip trailing zeros'
